extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and patent examiners (U.S. practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Official MPEP guidance describing the types of patent applications (utility/plant/design, national, provisional, international, continuation/divisional/CIP/CPA) and the statutory/regulatory filing, content, priority, and benefit-claiming requirements under U.S. law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable subject matter (35 U.S.C. 101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whoever invents or discovers any new and useful process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter, or any new and useful improvement thereof, may obtain a patent therefor, subject to the conditions and requirements of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the statutory categories of inventions that may be the subject of a patent: process, machine, manufacture, composition of matter, and improvements. (MPEP cites 35 U.S.C. 101.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant patents (35 U.S.C. 161)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whoever invents or discovers and asexually reproduces any distinct and new variety of plant... may obtain a patent therefor, subject to the conditions and requirements of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plant patents are governed by 35 U.S.C. 161; provisions relating to patents for inventions apply except as otherwise provided. (MPEP references Chapter 1600 for details.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patents (35 U.S.C. 171)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whoever invents any new, original, and ornamental design for an article of manufacture may obtain a patent therefor... The filing date of an application for patent for design shall be the date on which the specification as prescribed by section 112 and any required drawings are filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design patents have statutory distinctiveness and filing-date rule (specification and required drawings required for filing date). See MPEP Chapter 1500 for design procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three broad types of patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications can be directed to three broad types of subject matter: (A) applications under 35 U.S.C. 101 (utility), (B) plant patents under 35 U.S.C. 161, and (C) design patents under 35 U.S.C. 171.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility patents are often referred to as 'utility' applications in contrast to plant or design; design and plant applications have specialized procedures (Chapters 1500 and 1600).

rubrics_metrics.name: National application statutory content requirements (35 U.S.C. 111(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for patent shall be made in writing to the Director and shall include a specification as prescribed by section 112, a drawing as prescribed by section 113, and an oath or declaration as prescribed by section 115. The application must be accompanied by the fee required by law; fee, oath/declaration, and 1+ claims may be submitted after the filing date within prescribed periods and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit required fee/oath/claims within prescribed period results in abandonment. The filing date is the date a specification, with or without claims, is received in the USPTO (subject to later statutory/PLT amendments described).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application requirements (35 U.S.C. 111(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application shall include a specification as prescribed by section 112(a) and a drawing as prescribed by section 113; a claim is not required in a provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional apps: fee may be submitted after filing date within prescribed period; filing date is when specification (with or without claims) is received; provisional will be regarded as abandoned 12 months after filing if no timely request to treat it as a nonprovisional is made; provisional applications are not examined for patentability and are not entitled to priority under certain statutory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date definition (post-PLT/AIA context)
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of an application is the date on which a specification, with or without claims, is received in the USPTO; for design patents the filing date is when the specification including at least one claim and any required drawings are received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PLTIA (Dec 18, 2013) changed filing-date requirements for nonprovisional applications (see MPEP §§601.01 and 601.01(f)); nonprovisional utility and plant apps filed on/after that date may receive a filing date without claims or drawings, but design patent filing date rules remain stricter.

rubrics_metrics.name: No right of priority / benefit for provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application shall not be entitled to the right of priority of any other application under section 119, 365(a), or 386(a) or to the benefit of an earlier filing date in the United States under sections 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional applications cannot themselves serve as the basis for certain priority claims; a later nonprovisional may claim benefit of a provisional under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), but the provisional alone lacks certain priority rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director-prescribed treatment of prior-filed application reference for filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may prescribe conditions under which a reference upon the filing of an application to a previously filed application shall constitute the specification and drawings of the subsequent application for purposes of a filing date, provided a copy of the specification and drawings is submitted within prescribed period and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit the copy within the prescribed period results in abandonment; such an application is treated as never filed unless revived under section 27 and copy submitted. See 35 U.S.C. 111(c) and MPEP §601.01(a), subsection III.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.9 definitions of application types
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'national application', 'provisional application', 'nonprovisional application', 'international application', and 'international design application' for the chapter: e.g., a national application means a U.S. application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111, certain international applications with paid national fee, or international design applications with registration copy received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These regulatory definitions determine how various filing- and processing-rules apply (national stage treatment, filing-date effects, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Differences between nonprovisional and provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant differences include: (A) No claim required in provisional; (B) No oath/declaration required in provisional; (C) Provisionals are not examined for patentability; (D) Provisional is not entitled to claim priority to foreign apps or benefit of earlier national apps; (E) Design patent application is not entitled to claim the benefit of a provisional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §201.01 for detailed distinctions and see MPEP §201.04 for detailed provisional info.

rubrics_metrics.name: International application designating the United States has national effect (35 U.S.C. 363)
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application designating the United States shall have the effect, from its international filing date under article 11 of the treaty, of a national application for patent regularly filed in the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatment of national application under 35 U.S.C. 111 and national stage application are similar but not identical; see MPEP §1893.03 et seq. for national stage differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: International design application effect (35 U.S.C. 385)
rubrics_metrics.description: An international design application designating the United States shall have the effect, for all purposes, from its filing date determined in accordance with section 384, of an application for patent filed in the USPTO pursuant to chapter 16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP Chapter 2900 for information regarding international design applications and 37 CFR 1.9 definitions relating to Hague Agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute application definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'substitute' application is the duplicate of an application by the same applicant abandoned before the filing of the later application; a substitute does not obtain the benefit of the filing date of the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current practice does not require the applicant to insert in the specification a reference to the earlier application, but attention should be called to the earlier application; use form paragraph 2.07 to remind applicant of possible substitute status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing application categories and statutory bases
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) include original nonprovisional utility, plant, design, divisional, continuation, and continuation-in-part applications filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b), reissue applications under 1.53(b), and design CPAs under 1.53(d). Continuing applications are filed under the conditions in 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) and 37 CFR 1.78.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§201.06 et seq., 201.07, and 201.08 for divisional, continuation, and CIP specifics; see MPEP §211 et seq. for claiming benefit rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation application requirements (no new matter; inventorship; benefit claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation must not include any subject matter which would constitute new matter relative to the prior application; the inventorship must include at least one inventor named in the prior-filed application; the continuation must claim the benefit of the prior-filed application under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuation may be filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) (or 1.53(d) for CPAs in design context). See 37 CFR 1.78 and MPEP §211 et seq. for more information on entitlement to benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued Prosecution Application (CPA) practice limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d) is available only for design applications (not international design applications) and must be filed prior to payment of the issue fee unless a petition is granted in the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPAs are a special continued-prosecution vehicle for design practice; see MPEP §201.06(d) for CPA practice and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation-in-part (CIP) definition and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation-in-part is an application filed during the lifetime of a prior-filed application that repeats some substantial portion or all of the prior-filed application and adds matter not disclosed in the prior-filed application; it must claim benefit of the prior filing under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A CIP may only be filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b); it cannot be filed as a CPA. Requirements to claim benefit include same inventor or at least one common joint inventor, filing before patenting/abandonment of the prior application, and containing a specific reference to the earlier filed application (post-2012: reference in ADS). See MPEP §201.08 and §211.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content of benefit claims (37 CFR 1.78 / MPEP §211)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any nonprovisional application that claims the benefit of one or more prior-filed applications must contain or be amended to contain a reference to each such prior-filed application identifying it by application number, international application number and date, or international registration number and filing date; the reference must identify whether the later application is a continuation, divisional, or continuation-in-part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012, the specific reference must be included in an application data sheet (ADS) per 37 CFR 1.76(b)(5). See MPEP §211 for procedures to correct/add benefit claims and time limits under 37 CFR 1.78.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible derivation and inventorship rules for CIP
rubrics_metrics.description: A CIP that has a sole inventor may derive from an earlier application with joint inventors and disclose only a portion of the later application's subject matter, subject to conditions in 35 U.S.C. 120 and 37 CFR 1.78; similarly joint-inventor CIPs may derive from sole-inventor earlier apps under the same conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office does not need to determine satisfaction of 35 U.S.C. 112(a) for benefit of the earlier filing unless the earlier filing date is relied upon in a proceeding. See MPEP §201.08 for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional abandonment and non-revivability after 12 months
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application shall be regarded as abandoned 12 months after the filing date if no timely request is made to treat it as a nonprovisional application, and it shall not be subject to revival after such 12-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to section 119(e)(3) and Director-prescribed conditions for conversion/treatment; practitioners should timely convert or file a nonprovisional claiming benefit under 119(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction vs unity of invention practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction practice (MPEP §806 et seq.) is applied to national applications under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), while unity of invention practice (MPEP §§1850 and 1893.03(d)) is applied to national stage applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different multiplicity handling applies depending on whether the application is a domestic national application or a PCT national-stage application; practitioners must be aware of the appropriate practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete national and national-stage application notification practice distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: National nonprovisional applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) without an executed oath/declaration, basic filing fee, search fee, or examination fee are governed by the notification practice set forth in 37 CFR 1.53(f); incomplete national stage applications are governed by notification practice set forth in 37 CFR 1.495.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different procedures and notices are used for cure of missing parts depending on filing type and stage; consult the cited CFR provisions and MPEP sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application is not examined for patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional applications will not be examined for patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provisional primarily preserves a filing date and provides a 12-month window to file a corresponding nonprovisional; substantive examination occurs only in the later-filed nonprovisional (if timely filed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111 may include divisional, continuation, CIP, reissue, and CPAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) include original nonprovisional utility, plant, design, divisional, continuation, continuation-in-part applications filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b), reissue applications filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b), and design patent continued prosecution applications under 37 CFR 1.53(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§201.06, 201.07, and 201.08 for detailed procedures, and MPEP §601.01(a) for overview of filing under 35 U.S.C. 111.
